answer: In an issuer-sponsored tokenized security, the company—or its agent—issues the security directly on a blockchain. When it is the same class of security, it carries the same legal rights as a traditional share of that class, such as voting, dividends, and ownership. A tokenized security may instead belong to a different class from the company’s traditionally issued securities, so the class matters when considering its rights.
